doc.title: Ramsey Lewis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The trio at Chess and The In Crowd
title: The Lighthouse date and who handled the trio's business
summary: Brown confirms the October 1965 Lighthouse recording and January 1966 dissolution; Lewis says he wrote the music and did interviews while the others shared road chores.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: I’m looking at your discography. You recorded at the Lighthouse October ’65.
So by January ’66 the group was dissolved.
Can we go back to a couple things? One, when you first – before the band had a hit, were you doing all the business? Like you say, calling all the hotels, calling . . . ?

Yeah. I was the lead guy in terms of – I would write all the music and do all the interviews. I can’t recall if I was also calling hotels and lining up rental cars. I think they took care of the rental cars, because I didn’t get my driver’s license until after we were together and we were on the road. So the duties were split among all three of us. I was satisfied, just doing the music.
